messages.content: I need to start planning a Kansas City trip for a collection installation. I have to be there for a crate opening Tuesday morning, so I need to fly out of Atlanta on Monday. The return is less certain because the lender inspection is Thursday and I do not have its final time yet.

What dates are we working with, and how early is the Tuesday crate opening? I can compare Monday arrivals with enough margin and then lay out Thursday evening and Friday morning returns without selecting one yet.

The crate opening is Tuesday, January 12 at 9:00 a.m. Installation continues Wednesday. The inspection is Thursday, January 14, but right now it is only listed as sometime that afternoon. I would leave Atlanta Monday, January 11.
Understood. Is the art traveling with you in any form, or is this just your own luggage and work materials? That affects whether a tight airport transfer or checked-bag timing matters.
The shipment is going separately through the museum's carrier. I will have one checked suitcase and a small case of installation paperwork, nothing oversized.

I found three useful nonstop choices from Atlanta to Kansas City on Monday, January 11. Delta departs at 8:25 a.m. Eastern and arrives at 9:34 a.m. Central. Southwest departs at 10:40 a.m. and arrives at 11:55 a.m. Central. A later Delta flight leaves at 1:20 p.m. and arrives at 2:31 p.m. Central. All three leave ample time before Tuesday morning, though the first two preserve more recovery time if Monday operations are disrupted.
The 8:25 is earlier than I need. Compare the 10:40 and 1:20 more closely. Are they both nonstop, and what do the round trips look like with the possible returns?

Both are nonstop. The Southwest outbound includes two checked bags and has open seating assignment at check-in under its current fare terms. The Delta 1:20 p.m. option is Main Cabin, includes advance seat selection, and charges separately for the checked suitcase. For returns, I see Thursday nonstops at 6:15 p.m. and 8:35 p.m. Central, plus Friday nonstops at 7:10 a.m. and 9:25 a.m. Central. I can price the sensible pairings once we decide how much time you need between the inspection site and MCI.
The museum is near the Nelson-Atkins, and I would need to collect my suitcase from the hotel before going to the airport. Assume I should leave the museum two hours before departure.

With that assumption, the Thursday 6:15 p.m. flight requires you to leave the museum by about 4:15 p.m. That is vulnerable if the inspection starts late or runs more than an hour or two. The 8:35 p.m. flight moves the museum departure to about 6:35 p.m. and is much more workable. It arrives in Atlanta at 11:31 p.m. Eastern. Friday's 7:10 a.m. return arrives at 10:05 a.m. Eastern, while the 9:25 a.m. arrives at 12:20 p.m.
I agree that 6:15 Thursday is too exposed. Keep the 8:35 Thursday in the comparison. For Friday, use the 7:10 because if I stay the extra night I would rather get back before the middle of the day.

Using those two returns, the Southwest 10:40 a.m. Monday outbound pairs with the Thursday 8:35 p.m. return for $438 round trip, including the checked suitcase. The same outbound with the Friday 7:10 a.m. return is $402, but it adds a fourth hotel night. The Delta 1:20 p.m. Monday outbound pairs with Thursday at 8:35 p.m. for $421 in Main Cabin, or with Friday at 7:10 a.m. for $389. Delta's totals do not include the checked-bag charge.
Are all of those returns nonstop? Your wording makes it sound as though the same flights can be paired with either airline.

Good catch. They are all nonstop, but they are not the same operating flights. The Thursday 8:35 p.m. and Friday 7:10 a.m. times I just priced are Southwest. Delta's closest nonstop returns are Thursday at 8:10 p.m., arriving Atlanta at 11:06 p.m., and Friday at 7:35 a.m., arriving at 10:31 a.m. The corrected Delta round-trip totals are $421 for the Thursday 8:10 p.m. return and $389 for the Friday 7:35 a.m. return, before the checked-bag charge.

Thank you for correcting that. Does the Monday 1:20 Delta arrival still give me a reasonable cushion if there is a cancellation? I do not need to do any work Monday, but I cannot miss Tuesday at nine.

Its scheduled 2:31 p.m. Central arrival gives you more than 18 hours before the crate opening, which is comfortable for an ordinary delay. The risk is a cancellation late enough that same-day nonstop reaccommodation becomes limited. Delta has another Atlanta departure around 4:45 p.m., subject to seats, and connecting itineraries later in the day, so there are recovery paths but no guarantee. The Southwest 10:40 a.m. departure leaves more of Monday available for reaccommodation if operations deteriorate.
Then the 10:40 Southwest outbound is the stronger option for this job. What time would I reach Kansas City, and what are the complete totals again for the two return choices?

The Southwest outbound leaves Atlanta Monday, January 11 at 10:40 a.m. Eastern and reaches Kansas City at 11:55 a.m. Central. Paired with the Thursday, January 14 nonstop at 8:35 p.m. Central, arriving Atlanta at 11:31 p.m. Eastern, the current round-trip total is $438. Paired with the Friday, January 15 nonstop at 7:10 a.m. Central, arriving Atlanta at 10:05 a.m. Eastern, the airfare is $402. Both totals include taxes and your checked suitcase under the fare shown.

Is there any meaningful fare restriction between those two, or is the difference mainly the travel day? I do not want the cheaper Friday fare to be completely inflexible while we are waiting on the lender.

Both are the same standard Southwest fare type. Neither is refundable to the original form of payment, but each can be changed or canceled before departure for a reusable flight credit under the displayed rules, with any fare difference applying to a change. The $36 difference is tied to the return inventory, not a more restrictive fare category. No reservation has been made, so these prices can move while the inspection time remains unresolved.

That is enough for now. Do not choose or hold a return. Keep the Monday 10:40 outbound as the flight we are considering, and retain both the Thursday 8:35 evening return at $438 total and the Friday 7:10 morning return at $402 total. I should have the lender's inspection time shortly.

I have retained the planning comparison with nothing booked or held: Southwest nonstop from Atlanta to Kansas City on Monday, January 11, departing 10:40 a.m. Eastern and arriving 11:55 a.m. Central; paired either with the Thursday, January 14 return departing 8:35 p.m. Central and arriving 11:31 p.m. Eastern for $438 round trip, or the Friday, January 15 return departing 7:10 a.m. Central and arriving 10:05 a.m. Eastern for $402. Both current totals include taxes and one checked suitcase. The return remains undecided until the Thursday lender inspection time is confirmed, and fares will need to be rechecked then.
